findings.label: RELAY_URL with a bare ? or # slips through resolveRelay
findings.summary: src/relay.js:21 rejects parsed.search/parsed.hash, but WHATWG sets both to '' for a bare delimiter, so 'https://r.test/?' and 'https://r.test/#' are accepted silently and relayFeedUrl yields 'https://r.test/?/feed/importai'; every relay request then 404s and every viaRelay row reads 'relay: HTTP 404, fell back to direct' without the 'relay disabled:' warning.
findings.action: In resolveRelay reject a trimmed RELAY_URL that contains '?' or '#' (or require parsed.href === rawUrl after trailing-slash stripping) so the 'relay disabled:' warn fires; add 'https://r.test/?' and 'https://r.test/#' to the malformed-URL test in tests/relay.test.js.

findings.label: Token visible in Cloudflare request logs and saved tail captures
findings.summary: wrangler tail --format json and Workers Logs ([observability] enabled = true, relay/wrangler.toml:9-10) record event.request.headers for every invocation, which includes x-relay-token; FEAT-001 saved a tail capture to a file to parse it, so that file likely contains the token. Only the Cloudflare account owner can read either, so this is hygiene rather than a leak, but D10's 'never in a log' did not account for it.
findings.action: Capture one tail event and check event.request.headers; if x-relay-token is present, delete the FEAT-001 tail capture file, add one sentence to the README secret-hygiene paragraph (README.md:154) that Cloudflare's own request logs show the header to the account owner and tail output must not be saved or shared, and rotate the token if any capture was shared.

findings.label: README footprint arithmetic
findings.summary: README.md:152 states '8 cron ticks x 6 fetches plus about 16 relay requests x 4 scheduled runs, i.e. under 100 Worker requests'; 48 + 64 = 112. The 48 cron fetches are subrequests inside 8 cron invocations, so Worker requests are about 72/day.
findings.action: Reword the footprint sentence so the stated numbers add up (e.g. '8 cron invocations making 48 upstream subrequests, plus about 64 pipeline requests, i.e. roughly 72 Worker requests/day').

findings.label: Relay-then-direct timing is reasoned, not tested
findings.summary: The D9 comment at src/http.js:290-293 (15 s relay timeout + 20 s direct timeout + 2 s backoff = 37 s, no second direct attempt because 8 s < 25 s remain) has no fakeClock test through runSource; the Worker's 429 worst case (slow first 429 + 2 s + 10 s second attempt exceeding the pipeline's 15 s relay timeout) is also untested.
findings.action: Optional: add one pipeline test with fakeClock where the relay times out at 15 s and the direct fetch at 20 s, asserting the direct error has attempts === 1 and the row's ms stays under 45_000.
